metaTitle: Cert III Individual Support Fast Track RPL (CHC33021)
metaDescription: Aged care or disability worker? Fast track your CHC33021 Cert III in Individual Support with RPL. Online, no classes, 4–8 weeks. Free eligibility check.
heroIntro: The CHC33021 Certificate III in Individual Support is the main entry qualification for aged care and disability support work in Australia. If you're already providing personal care, RPL recognises that experience, so you get qualified without stopping work or sitting through classes.
whoIsItFor:
RPL is for support workers who already do the job:

  • Personal care workers and assistants in nursing (AINs) in residential aged care
  • Home care and community care workers
  • NDIS disability support workers
  • Overseas-trained carers and nurses working in support roles
  • Workers whose employer now requires a formal qualification

The qualification has ageing, disability and home and community specialisations. You'll need recent experience providing person-centred support such as personal care, mobility assistance, meals, social support and following care plans. It includes 120 hours of work in the industry, which your current job can cover.
evidenceExamples:
• A reference or statement of service from your employer or a registered nurse describing your duties
  • Your position description and payslips showing time in a care role
  • Training certificates: manual handling, infection control, medication assistance, first aid and CPR
  • Examples of progress notes or shift reports you've written (with client details removed)
  • Your NDIS Worker Screening Check, police check or Working with Children Check, if held

An assessor will also usually observe you at work or talk to your supervisor to confirm your skills.
licensingInfo: Support work isn't licensed, but employers and funding schemes set their own requirements. Many aged care providers now expect a Certificate III, and NDIS workers in risk-assessed roles need an NDIS Worker Screening Check. A police check is standard across the sector.
description:
The CHC33021 Certificate III in Individual Support covers providing person-centred support to older people and people with disability, in residential care, community and home settings. It includes personal care, safe work practices, communication, supporting independence and wellbeing, infection control, and following an individualised plan.

Specialisations in ageing, disability, or home and community care are chosen through electives, and through RPL they're matched to the work you already do.
jobOpportunity: Personal care worker / assistant in nursing (aged care)
imageAlt: Aged care worker supporting an elderly resident

faqs.q: Can I get the CHC33021 Certificate III in Individual Support through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you're working in aged care, disability or home care. Your duties, references, training certificates and a workplace observation are assessed against the units.
Most people finish in 4 to 8 weeks.

faqs.q: Can I do it online while I work?
faqs.a: Yes. Your evidence and interview are online, and your workplace observation is arranged around your shifts. You don't need to stop working.

faqs.q: Do I still need the 120 work placement hours?
faqs.a: The qualification requires 120 hours of work in the industry. If you're already working in a care role, those hours come from your job, so you don't need a separate placement.
It depends on your experience and any gap training. RPL usually costs less than full study. Start with a free eligibility check.

faqs.q: Ageing, disability or home and community: which specialisation should I choose?
faqs.a: Choose the one that matches your work. If you work across sectors, we'll help you pick electives that cover both. Many people later go on to the Certificate IV in Ageing Support or the Certificate IV in Disability Support.

faqs.q: I'm an overseas nurse. Can I use RPL?
faqs.a: Yes. Overseas nursing or care experience can count toward this qualification, alongside Australian work experience.

  • Youth program plans and evaluations
  • Your Working with Children Check
  • A reference from your manager
licensingInfo: Working with young people requires a current Working with Children Check.
description: The CHC50425 Diploma of Youth Work covers working with young people: case work, developing and running youth programs, supporting young people at risk, working with families and communities, and youth-centred, culturally safe practice.
imageAlt: Youth worker mentoring a young person

faqs.q: What replaced CHC50421 Diploma of Youth Work?
faqs.a: CHC50421 has been superseded by CHC50425 Diploma of Youth Work. If you already hold CHC50421 it stays valid. New enrolments and RPL are in CHC50425.

faqs.q: Can I get the Diploma of Youth Work through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you have youth work experience. Your de-identified case work, program plans and references are assessed against the units.
Usually 6 to 10 weeks.
It depends on your evidence. Start with a free eligibility check.

faqs.q: Is a CHC50425 gained through RPL the same as studying it?
faqs.a: Yes. It is the same nationally recognised CHC50425 Diploma of Youth Work, issued by a registered training organisation. Your certificate and transcript don’t say whether you got it through RPL or by studying.

metaTitle: CHC30221 Cert III Education Support RPL — Teacher Aide
metaDescription: Working as a teacher aide? Get the CHC30221 Certificate III in School Based Education Support through RPL using your classroom experience. Free check.
heroIntro: The CHC30221 Certificate III in School Based Education Support is the entry qualification for teacher aides and education assistants. If you already support students in the classroom, RPL recognises that experience so you get the qualification without starting a course from scratch.
whoIsItFor:
• Teacher aides and education assistants in primary or secondary schools
  • Learning support officers and integration aides
  • School volunteers with regular, structured classroom roles
  • Education support workers who trained overseas

You'll usually have at least six to twelve months working in a school, supporting literacy and numeracy, helping students with additional needs, supervising students and following school policies.
evidenceExamples:
• A reference or statement of service from the school principal or your supervising teacher
  • Examples of learning activities or resources you've prepared (with student details removed)
  • Records of reading, literacy or numeracy support sessions you've run
  • Training certificates, such as child protection, first aid or behaviour support
  • Your Working with Children Check

The qualification includes 100 hours of work placement. If you already work in a school, those hours can usually be completed and verified in your current role.
description:
The CHC30221 Certificate III in School Based Education Support covers the skills to support teachers and students in schools: meeting legal and ethical obligations, contributing to educational programs, supporting literacy, oral language and numeracy, supporting students with additional needs, supporting responsible behaviour, contributing to student health and safety, and working with diverse people.

The higher-level qualification is the Certificate IV in School Based Education Support.

faqs.q: Can I get a teacher aide qualification through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you already work or volunteer regularly in a school. A reference from your school, examples of your work and your training records are assessed against the units.

faqs.q: Do I need to do work placement?
faqs.a: The qualification requires 100 hours of work placement in a school. If you already work in one, those hours can usually be verified in your current role.
Usually 4 to 8 weeks, depending on your evidence and when your workplace can verify your skills.

faqs.q: Should I do the Certificate III or Certificate IV?
faqs.a: If you are newer to the role, the Certificate III is the usual starting point. If you have several years of experience and work more independently, including with students with additional needs, the Certificate IV may suit you better.
The cost depends on how much your evidence covers. RPL is usually much cheaper than full study. Start with a free eligibility check.
